# Atomtronic Isolation Quantum Limits

> Exact accessible-channel boundary and quantum-rate limits for a linear
> atomtronic scatterer with two positive ports, inaccessible idlers, and a
> source-collected return. The complete account is organized by topic.

## Entry and story
- [README](README.md): principal results, example, reading routes and contact.
- [Model](science/model.md): modes, parties, capacities, assumptions and claims.
- [Interpretation](science/interpretation.md): what classical isolation
  certifies, experimental calibration, resources and changed interfaces.

## Learning route
- [Learning overview](learning/README.md): self-directed reading routes.
- [Weedbrook bridge](learning/WEEDBROOK_BRIDGE.md): the single educational
  anchor, precise arXiv-v1 section pointers, quadrature conversion, a worked
  collection-threshold example, and the missing steps to the project results.
- [Thirty milestones](learning/MILESTONES.md): M01–M13 are background;
  M14–M30 reconstruct the contribution. Each phase runs from local ingredients
  to global understanding, with distinct targets and earlier dependencies.
- State/channel foundations: M01–M11. Complete resource model: M12–M13.
  Exact boundary and arbitrary-input proof: M17–M20. Rate comparison:
  M16 and M21–M23. Atomic and packet accounting: M24–M29. Synthesis: M30.
- The common map contains no personal assessment procedure or learner records.
  It does not replace the exact statements and proofs in science/.

## Questions and authoritative answers
- When does every protocol fail, including non-Gaussian adaptive protocols?
  [Collection boundary](science/collection_boundary.md): exact condition,
  infinite-dimensional sender instrument, adversary model, finite-energy
  achievability, thermal extension and degenerate cases.
- How do rates scale with reverse power?
  [Communication rates](science/communication_rates.md): reduced-channel
  quadratic upper envelope, ideal-return Theta(R) family, bounded-energy
  protocol and full-channel logarithmic-negativity proof.
- What does commutator preservation require? Can another port evade it?
  [Scattering and noise](science/scattering_noise.md): receiver floor, sharp
  positive-output noise sum, source-noise tradeoff and additional-port bound.
- Is there an atomic Hamiltonian and is it stable?
  [Stable atomic model](science/stable_atomic_model.md): scattering, ring
  collisions, drive phases, pump/reference/port assumptions and atom flux.
- What changes for a finite-duration pulse?
  [Finite bandwidth](science/finite_bandwidth.md): whole-band impossibility,
  temporal auxiliaries, corrected reverse resource and finite-packet witness.

## Essential distinctions
- Discarded and sender-accessible reflection define different channels.
  A zero channel across Alice/Bob may retain quantum information at Alice.
- R is reverse power, not amplitude. G is forward power and N is receiver
  vacuum-output occupation. Vacuum quadrature covariance is I/2; the selected
  review uses I. Change quadrature ordering separately from normalization.
- The vacuum zero region is c=N-G >= 0 and (1-eta)c >= eta R, including
  equality. Collection precedes every usable source operation.
- The reduced-channel O(R^2) expression is an upper bound. Ideal collection
  for the stable family has matched Theta(R) order, not a known exact
  capacity. Logarithmic negativity bounds Q2, not general secret key.
- All-input converses include squeezed and non-Gaussian signal encodings.
  Their justification is the local-instrument construction, not an arbitrary
  extrapolation from a covariance test. A phase-sensitive device changes the model.
- Gaussian monitoring does not imply Gaussian-only entanglement distillation.
- Positive-output occupation sums do not count the idler. Per-mode rates
  do not determine rates per second. Finite-pump and finite-band errors must
  be controlled relative to the shrinking entanglement margin.
- Gaussian feedback and amplifier-noise principles are prior art.
  The related-work account states the limits of the comparison.
